Section: M3-PREFLIGHT-001 — executable Workbench preparation > Executed ordering
Each requested semantic interval executes native `step` exactly once. Discovery may prepare a complete component. Main reserves a real disabled body and shapes, then sends the exact reservation acknowledgement. Native commit leaves inventory in `CommittedInactive`. Main installs touched static terrain contents and returns actual installed digests; native applies the occupancy mask. Only then does main activate the body and native acknowledge `BodyActivated`. Native geometry changes require main installation and the corresponding native geometry receipt before physical motion. One Rapier interval is divided into the same bounded real substeps as 001R. `advance_motion_segment` performs exactly one solver piece, publishes sampled poses and enters `AwaitingNative`. Main submits those poses to worker-owned `accept_motion`; only an exact applied receipt with unchanged semantic tick and full owner/pose inventory permits another solver piece. Maximum 16 segments and the original motion guards remain intact. Delayed replies leave both the UI and cancellation/reset controls live, without stepping physics again. The bridge requires an explicit completed native tick and refuses duplicate/backward ticks or reused native sessions. The synchronous wrapper and asynchronous API share this state machine. A retained-action control matched all 3,599 before/after pose rows and accounting against the unchanged final001R bridge on the same pinned native runtime; extraction did not invent a second dynamics implementation. A preparation cancellation retains World inventory and removes only uncommitted reservations. It then finishes the physical interval belonging to the native tick that already ran. An actual negative reproduced the old skipped interval (native2→3 while physics4→4); the maintained adverse case covers the repair. Reset retires pending transport sequences, requests explicit native whole-session disposal and reinitializes main RIDs only after the new session receipt. A late receipt during Closing/Closed is nonmutating; duplicate worker stop preserves its original terminal result. Stop refusal leaves the native owner/thread retained with a visible `ShutdownHeld` reason.

A failed host stays Held until explicit native whole-session reset or stop. Cancellation, promotion resume, idle scheduling and transport continuations cannot resume chemistry, Rapier or queued edits while failed. A 15-second missing-receipt deadline retains actual owners and exposes the pending operation. Expiry does not authorize replay of an uncertain mutation. A reset whose successful receipt was lost can leave worker and host sessions different. Recovery reads the worker session solely to request another explicit disposal. It cannot authorize edits, adopt an unseen snapshot or activate old RIDs. The worker atomically refuses a second reset while one is queued or executing, including when full control replies prevent its start. Only a fresh successful reset receipt with a strictly newer native session reinitializes main physics. Bounded terminal input records survive reset in `retired_action_results` and incident exports. They distinguish exact queued cancellation from an in-flight outcome that cannot be reconstructed. The old trace retains retirement events before the next session starts its own trace; uncertain mutation traces cannot claim a successful complete replay. An in-place `Host.reset` intentionally retains native allocation generations and the bridge pose serial. Its new trace declares `standalone_replay: false` and `inherited-native-registry`; the standalone replayer refuses it before constructing a new owner. Reproducing that history needs the preceding sessions, which this driver does not reconstruct. The interactive scene's Reset/scenario path instead disposes and recreates the worker/host. Those fresh-registry traces can replay even when their process-global native session number is not one: only the header's current session is mapped to the new session, preserving every body, generation, pose, cell and material witness. Stale targets must still be refused. Continuous pointer admission uses the publication actually presented to the view. The scene offers input an admission opportunity before scheduling the next interval from that displayed tick. This makes fresh moving cuts usable while preserving exact pose/material/geometry refusal for stale commands and the native debit fence.
